questions.question: What should you do BEFORE a listening passage starts?
options: Read the questions, predict content and identify key words
Close your eyes and relax
Write a full summary in advance
Translate the questions to Norwegian
questions.explanation: In the before-phase you read the questions, predict the content and identify key words so you know what to listen for.

questions.question: What does it mean to listen "for gist"?
options: Listening for the overall meaning before focusing on details
Writing down every word you hear
Only listening to the first sentence
Listening for grammar mistakes
questions.explanation: Listening for gist means catching the overall meaning first — then you listen again for specific details.

questions.question: What is "connected speech"?
options: Words blending together in natural speech, like "Whaddya want?"
Speaking with a cable microphone
Two people speaking at once
Reading a text aloud slowly
questions.explanation: In natural speech words blend: "What do you want?" becomes "Whaddya want?" — a challenge for listeners.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss a word during a listening task?
options: Use context to fill the gap — you do not need to catch every word
Stop listening and give up on the question
Ask the examiner to restart the recording
Guess randomly without thinking
questions.explanation: Good listeners use context to fill in gaps and keep following the passage rather than getting stuck on one word.

questions.question: How can you get better at understanding different English accents?
options: Expose yourself regularly to films, podcasts and videos with varied accents
Only listen to your own teacher
Avoid all non-British media
Read more books silently
questions.explanation: Regular exposure to British, American, Australian, Indian and African accents trains your ear for variety.
